messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The bug report explains that the equality test for multi-valued variables in JXPath does not conform to the specification. Specifically, when a variable such as d={ "a", "b" } (an array of strings) is tested against a value, e.g., "$d = 'a'", the expected behavior per the spec is that the comparison should be true if any element of the multi-valued variable equals the value, i.e., it should iterate over the components of the array and test each element. However, the current implementation compares the entire array object directly against the string, causing the comparison to fail.

The failing test method testIterateVariable has an assertion that "$d = 'a'" evaluates to true (Boolean.TRUE) but according to the bug report, this test fails because the == equals comparison is done on the variable's immediate content (the array itself), not iterating over the array elements.

Looking at the relevant code snippet in VariablePointer.equals(Object), the comparison checks identity and class equality, then compares fields:

```java
return variables == other.variables
    && name.equals(other.name)
    && index == other.index;
```

This equality method does not deal with the content of the variable value itself, nor does it iterate over the elements when the variable is multi-valued (array or collection). The root cause is that VariablePointer's equals method is doing a shallow comparison or reference comparison rather than value-wise or element-wise comparison required for multi-valued variables.

There is no direct evidence in the provided snippets of how XPath expressions like "$d = 'a'" are evaluated, but it is logical that the comparison operation relies on VariablePointer.equals or some similar equality method.

The recent bug reports do not contain significant insights or relevant fixes for such multi-valued variable equality issues, so they can be ignored for this diagnosis.

Summary: The bug arises because VariablePointer.equals does not implement element-wise comparison for multi-valued variables, causing the expression "$d = 'a'" to be evaluated as false even though "a" is inside variable "d"'s values.

The fix should involve adjusting the equality comparison logic for VariablePointer or wherever the variable value equality is tested, to conform to spec by iterating over the components of the multi-valued variable instead of comparing the array or collection object directly.

Next, I will determine the best class and method to fix based on these findings.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
